questions.question: Vasco da Gama reached India by sea in 1498. What did that route destroy?
options: The last remaining Arab shipbuilding industry along the coast
Portugal's own established trade agreements with West Africa
The overland spice monopoly held by Venice and the Ottomans
The entire Chinese trading presence across the Indian Ocean
questions.answer: The overland spice monopoly held by Venice and the Ottomans
questions.explanation: Spices had come overland through Ottoman-controlled territory to Venetian merchants, who set prices. A sea route around Africa cut both out, and Venice went into long decline as a result. Portugal built a chain of fortified trading posts rather than territorial colonies. Da Gama's first voyage lost roughly half its crew to scurvy, and the return cargo still sold for many times the cost of the entire expedition.
questions.memory_hook: Spices came overland through Ottoman land to Venetian traders who set the price. Sailing round Africa cut both out, and Venice declined from there. Da Gama lost about half his crew to scurvy, and the cargo he brought back still paid for the whole voyage many times over.

questions.question: The Sun's surface is around 5,500°C. What is strange about its outer atmosphere?
options: It is cool enough that water ice forms at its outer edge
It contains no hydrogen despite the core being full of it
The corona is far hotter than the surface beneath it
It rotates in the opposite direction to the Sun itself
questions.answer: The corona is far hotter than the surface beneath it
questions.explanation: The corona reaches over a million degrees while the surface sits near 5,500, which is like standing further from a fire and feeling hotter. This is the coronal heating problem and it is not fully solved, though magnetic reconnection and wave heating are the leading explanations. NASA's Parker Solar Probe was built to fly through the corona and measure it directly, and has now passed within about 6 million kilometres of the surface.
questions.memory_hook: The corona is over a million degrees while the surface is 5,500, which is like moving away from a fire and getting hotter. Nobody has fully solved why. Magnetic reconnection is the leading idea, and the Parker Solar Probe was built to fly through it and find out.

questions.question: New Zealand has won the Rugby World Cup three times. What do the All Blacks do before every match?
options: Circle the pitch once in complete silence together
Sing the national anthem entirely in Maori language
Perform the haka, a Maori ceremonial challenge
Touch a ceremonial stone carried by the team captain
questions.answer: Perform the haka, a Maori ceremonial challenge
questions.explanation: The haka is a Maori posture dance and the team has performed one since 1888. Ka Mate is the traditional version; Kapa o Pango, introduced in 2005, was written specifically for the team. Opposing sides must face it and have handled that differently, from advancing on it to ignoring it entirely, and World Rugby has occasionally fined teams for how they responded. The team's Maori name is Te Mana.
questions.memory_hook: A Maori posture dance the team has done since 1888. Ka Mate is the traditional one; Kapa o Pango was written for the team in 2005. Opponents have to stand and face it, and have variously advanced on it, ignored it, or been fined for how they reacted.

questions.question: Lost in Translation (2003) is built around two people in a Tokyo hotel. What was famously left unresolved?
options: What Bob whispers to Charlotte in the closing scene
Which of the two is narrating the film throughout
Whether the entire encounter happened only in a dream
Whether either character ever actually leaves Japan
questions.answer: What Bob whispers to Charlotte in the closing scene
questions.explanation: Bill Murray improvised the line and it was deliberately mixed below audibility. Coppola has said even she does not know exactly what he said, and that it was meant to belong to the two characters. She wrote the part for Murray and pursued him for months with no agent involved, since he had no manager and only a phone line. She won the Oscar for Original Screenplay.
questions.memory_hook: Murray improvised it and it was mixed under the audio on purpose. Coppola says even she does not know exactly what he said and that it belongs to the characters. She wrote the part for him and chased him for months, since he had no agent, only an answering machine.

questions.question: Madagascar split from Africa around 160 million years ago. What did that isolation produce?
options: The only island ecosystem with no flowering plants
A landscape with no native mammals of any kind at all
Around 90% of its wildlife exists nowhere else on Earth
Species almost identical to those on mainland Africa
questions.answer: Around 90% of its wildlife exists nowhere else on Earth
questions.explanation: Roughly 90% of Madagascar's wildlife is endemic, and the figure runs higher in some groups: about 92% of mammals, 95% of reptiles and over 99% of amphibians occur nowhere else, along with 89% of plants. All 100-plus lemur species are found only there, evolved from ancestors that probably rafted across on vegetation. There are no native monkeys, big cats or antelope, so lemurs occupy niches those animals fill elsewhere. Around 90% of the island's original forest cover has been cleared.
questions.memory_hook: About 90% of its wildlife exists nowhere else, and higher in some groups: 92% of mammals, 95% of reptiles, over 99% of amphibians. Every lemur species is Malagasy, descended from ancestors that likely rafted over on vegetation. No native monkeys or big cats, so lemurs took those roles instead.

questions.question: Truman ordered the atomic bombings in 1945. When did he learn the bomb existed?
options: During his time in the Senate, chairing a wartime committee
After Roosevelt died, having been vice president for weeks
At the Potsdam Conference, from Churchill rather than his own staff
Two years earlier, as one of the programme's original overseers
questions.answer: After Roosevelt died, having been vice president for weeks
questions.explanation: Truman had been vice president for 82 days and was not told about the Manhattan Project until after Roosevelt's death in April 1945. He learned of it from Secretary of War Stimson within days of taking office. He had chaired a Senate committee investigating wartime spending and had noticed unexplained expenditure, but had been warned off. He gave the order roughly four months after first hearing the project existed.
questions.memory_hook: He had been vice president for 82 days and nobody had told him the Manhattan Project existed. Stimson briefed him days after Roosevelt died. He had actually noticed the unexplained spending as a senator and been warned off. Four months later he gave the order.

questions.question: Musk founded SpaceX in 2002 with no aerospace background. What was the original plan?
options: Buy Russian missiles cheaply, then build rockets after refusal
Partner with Boeing to build a commercial launch division
Buy a defunct European launch company and restart it
License NASA technology and manufacture it more cheaply
questions.answer: Buy Russian missiles cheaply, then build rockets after refusal
questions.explanation: Musk went to Moscow intending to buy refurbished ICBMs to launch a greenhouse to Mars as a publicity stunt for space exploration. He was rebuffed and reportedly spat at, and concluded on the flight home that building rockets from scratch would be cheaper. SpaceX nearly failed after three consecutive launch failures, with the fourth succeeding on the last money the company had. It later made orbital boosters reusable, which nobody had done.
questions.memory_hook: He went to Moscow to buy refurbished ICBMs to send a greenhouse to Mars as a publicity stunt, got refused and reportedly spat at, and worked out on the flight home he could build rockets cheaper. Three launches failed, the fourth worked on the last of the money.

questions.question: Inertia is an object's resistance to changing motion. What does it depend on?
options: Both the mass and the surface area facing forward
Weight, which changes with gravitational field strength
Mass alone, regardless of size, shape or material
The material's density and its internal temperature
questions.answer: Mass alone, regardless of size, shape or material
questions.explanation: Inertia is determined purely by mass. Weight is mass times gravity and changes on the Moon, but inertia does not, so a heavy object is exactly as hard to shove sideways in orbit as on Earth even though it floats. Newton's first law states that motion continues unchanged without an external force, which contradicts everyday intuition only because friction and air resistance are always present.
questions.memory_hook: Only mass. Weight changes on the Moon but inertia does not, so shoving a heavy crate sideways in orbit is exactly as hard as on Earth even though it floats. Newton's first law feels wrong only because friction is always quietly acting.

questions.question: The Gobi is a cold desert, not a hot one. What is it best known for producing?
options: The world's largest deposits of high-grade copper ore
The last wild population of Bactrian camels in captivity
Dinosaur fossils, including the first eggs ever identified
A rare salt harvested only in the coldest winter months
questions.answer: Dinosaur fossils, including the first eggs ever identified
questions.explanation: Roy Chapman Andrews's 1920s expeditions found the first recognised dinosaur eggs at the Flaming Cliffs, along with Velociraptor and Protoceratops. The dry climate and exposed sandstone make it one of the richest fossil regions anywhere, including the famous fighting dinosaurs specimen preserving the two locked together. The Gobi is also expanding, driven by overgrazing and drought, which is why China planted a shelterbelt of trees along its edge.
questions.memory_hook: Roy Chapman Andrews found the first recognised dinosaur eggs there in the 1920s, plus Velociraptor and Protoceratops. Dry air and exposed sandstone make it one of the best fossil sites anywhere, including the two dinosaurs preserved mid-fight. It is also spreading, which is why China planted a tree belt.

questions.question: Saigon fell in 1975 and was renamed. What was the final American evacuation like?
options: A negotiated withdrawal completed over several calm weeks
Helicopters lifted from a rooftop while crowds pressed below
A naval evacuation from the coast under sustained fire
An airlift from the main airport with no civilians present
questions.answer: Helicopters lifted from a rooftop while crowds pressed below
questions.explanation: Operation Frequent Wind evacuated around 7,000 people in about 24 hours, and the photograph of a queue up a ladder to a rooftop helicopter became the war's closing image, though it was an apartment building rather than the embassy as often assumed. Helicopters were pushed off carrier decks into the sea to make room for more arriving. Many South Vietnamese who had worked with the Americans were left behind.
questions.memory_hook: About 7,000 people in 24 hours. The famous photo of the ladder to the rooftop helicopter was an apartment block, not the embassy as everyone assumes. They shoved helicopters off carrier decks into the sea to make landing room. Many who had worked with the Americans were left behind.

questions.question: Tom Cruise returned as Maverick 36 years later. What did he insist on for the sequel?
options: Removing all computer effects from the finished cut
Real jets with actors filmed in the air, not on a soundstage
Shooting the entire film in a single continuous location
Performing every aerial stunt himself in the pilot's seat
questions.answer: Real jets with actors filmed in the air, not on a soundstage
questions.explanation: Cruise refused green screen and had the cast trained through a months-long flight programme so they could withstand the G-forces while cameras recorded them inside real F/A-18s. He could not fly the fighter jets himself, since the Navy does not permit civilians to pilot them, though he flew other aircraft in the film. The film grossed over $1.4 billion and is credited with drawing audiences back to cinemas after the pandemic.
questions.memory_hook: No green screen. The cast went through months of flight training so they could take the G-forces while cameras rolled inside real F/A-18s. Cruise could not pilot the fighters himself, since the Navy will not allow civilians, though he flew other aircraft. It made over $1.4 billion.

questions.question: The Australian Open opens the tennis season in January. What forced a major change there?
options: Player strikes over prize money in the late 1990s
A rule change requiring all matches to be played indoors
Extreme heat, which now triggers a formal suspension policy
Bushfire smoke, which led to matches moving to another city
questions.answer: Extreme heat, which now triggers a formal suspension policy
questions.explanation: January in Melbourne regularly exceeds 40C and court surface temperatures have been recorded above 60C. Players have vomited, hallucinated and collapsed, and a ball boy fainted during one match. The tournament introduced a heat stress scale and roofs on its main courts. Smoke from the 2019-20 bushfires also disrupted qualifying, with one player retiring mid-match after a coughing fit, though matches were not relocated.
questions.memory_hook: Melbourne in January regularly passes 40C, with court surfaces recorded above 60. Players have vomited, hallucinated and collapsed. There is now a formal heat scale and roofs on the main courts. Bushfire smoke also disrupted qualifying in 2020.
